A nation’s future is shaped by the quality of its institutions and the courage of those who build them. Some leaders create successful enterprises. Others develop institutions that influence how societies think, make decisions and pursue progress. The latter leave something particularly valuable: opportunities for people they may never meet. Following Frank Aigbogun’s celebration of his 70th birthday on November 1, 2026, which I could not attend, I take immense pride in honouring a distinguished TEXEM alumnus, an exceptional media entrepreneur, an accomplished journalist and a remarkable Nigerian whose contributions to national development extend far beyond the newsroom. Frank’s life offers an inspiring lesson in purposeful leadership. His journey demonstrates that intellectual curiosity, enterprise, perseverance and a commitment to the public good can combine to create enduring national value. Beginning his journalism career at The Guardian in 1982, Frank subsequently worked with the Associated Press and Vanguard, where he rose to significant editorial responsibilities. These experiences prepared him for an undertaking that would reshape Nigerian business journalism. In 2001, he co-founded BusinessDay, recognising the need for a publication dedicated to serious economic reporting, corporate governance, financial markets and public policy. What followed was an extraordinary exercise in institution building. BusinessDay developed into one of Nigeria’s foremost platforms for business intelligence and economic debate, helping executives, investors, policymakers and citizens engage with issues central to national prosperity. Peter Drucker, the influential management thinker, observed, “The purpose of information is not knowledge. It is being able to take the right action.” Few observations better capture the importance of Frank’s contribution. Reliable economic journalism informs investment decisions, improves public understanding and creates opportunities to scrutinise government policies. Where credible information flourishes, accountability is stronger. Frank’s commitment to nation-building is equally evident in his involvement with the Nigerian Economic Summit Group. His 19 years of membership, including ten years of board service, contributed to the sustained engagement between the private sector and government that Nigeria needs for meaningful economic reform. His leadership as Chairman of the Board of Trustees of the Impact Investors Foundation further demonstrates his interest in linking investment, enterprise and positive social outcomes. Yet perhaps one of Frank’s most significant contributions is the professional talent he has helped develop. Through BusinessDay, journalists, analysts and editors have gained opportunities to sharpen their abilities and contribute to public discourse. Albert Einstein famously observed, “The important thing is not to stop questioning. Curiosity has its own reason for existence.” That spirit of inquiry is indispensable to responsible journalism. It encourages professionals to challenge assumptions, examine evidence and pursue understanding. Frank’s professional journey illustrates how curiosity, supported by discipline and sound judgement, can become a foundation for lasting institutional achievement. His accomplishments also offer an important lesson about good governance. Independent journalism strengthens democracy when it encourages transparency, examines public decisions and gives citizens reliable information with which to hold institutions accountable. Nelson Mandela expressed this responsibility powerfully: “A critical, independent and investigative press is the lifeblood of any democracy.” As Nigeria confronts complex economic choices, this principle’s relevance cannot be overstated. Strong institutions require scrutiny. Responsible policymaking requires evidence. Sustainable prosperity requires citizens and leaders who understand the consequences of their decisions. As Founder of TEXEM, UK, I find Frank’s remarkable achievements particularly gratifying because he is a valued member of our distinguished alum community. His journey embodies the commitment to strategic leadership, good governance, intellectual development, societal responsibility and nation-building that TEXEM seeks to encourage. The TEXEM alum community is enriched by accomplished leaders such as Frank, whose professional contributions show what can emerge when expertise is matched with dedication to the wider public interest. At 70, Frank’s achievements deserve admiration, but his example also invites reflection. How many institutions are we strengthening? Whose opportunities are we expanding? What knowledge are we passing to those who will lead after us? These questions matter because enduring leadership is measured through the value that continues to benefit society long after individual achievements have been celebrated. Dear Frank, on this magnificent milestone, I celebrate your courage, your intellectual contributions, your entrepreneurial accomplishments and your dedication to building institutions that matter. May the years ahead bring abundant good health, happiness, renewed energy and deeper fulfilment. May you continue to inspire younger generations, shape important national conversations and enjoy the immense satisfaction of seeing the people and institutions you have supported flourish. On behalf of TEXEM, UK, and our global alum community, I congratulate you wholeheartedly on your 70th birthday. May your next chapter be your most fulfilling yet, and may the institutions you have strengthened continue to enlarge the possibilities of our nation. Happy 70th birthday, Frank. Keep flourishing, keep inspiring and keep making a difference. Abubakre is the Founder, TEXEM, UK Kindly share this story:
